These are all above or very near the chance thresholds for their sample sizes. If the instruments were truly independent, such systematic pairwise agreement—even at fixed lags—should not recur. The 3-day offset between lab instruments and the 4–6-day offset involving observatory readings hint that the coupling may be mediated by environmental state changes that propagate on different timescales to different locations or measurement types.

hypotheses.rationale: All four instruments show high distinctness (98–95 unique values in 96–108 readings, minimum spacing 0.0001 in all cases), ruling out coarse quantization. The fact that exact repetition is negligible (longest run: 1 reading) argues against digital glitches, but does not rule out subtle systematic bias in how readings are derived from raw sensor data. hypotheses.label: Random noise with spurious patterns at small sample sizes; all correlations are statistical flukes
